american.prompt: Identify a familiar definition of fairness in a form or meeting. Which rule serves the purpose, and what else would make participation usable?

minnesota.prompt: Examine whether a familiar meeting practice treats silence as agreement. What would make the decision process clearer to each participant?

somali.prompt: Review an interpreter request and a name field. What language and name arrangement does the person ask for, and can the form record it accurately?

hmong.prompt: A person wants supporters at a meeting. Ask whom they want present, how they want to participate and which communication support they prefer.

karen.prompt: A referral lists a country but not a requested language. Ask the person what language and communication support they want before arranging interpretation.

african-american.prompt: Examine a housing-support criterion and ask what evidence it serves, who may face unnecessary burdens and which alternatives need review.

latino.prompt: A translated notice is offered in one language. Ask each participant which language or communication format actually works, including any requested interpreter support.

tribal-nations.prompt: For a proposed action with possible Tribal implications, follow the standing deference and contact the person or area responsible for Tribal relations; distinguish consultation from a general listening event.

alaska-native.prompt: For substantive questions concerning Native people or communities, follow the existing standing deference and seek guidance from the people or areas responsible rather than inferring a Nation’s position.

european-american.prompt: Identify an office practice that seems neutral to you. What does it reward, and what other usable ways to contribute might meet the same purpose?

rural.prompt: An online meeting has low attendance. Examine scheduling, access to technology and other participation options before drawing conclusions about interest.

russian-speaking.prompt: A form equates a language request with nationality. Remove that inference and ask only the information needed to provide the requested support.

arabic-speaking.prompt: Before scheduling or interpreting, ask each person about communication, language and availability rather than inferring religion or observance from a language.

oromo.prompt: A language request is unclear in an appointment workflow. Confirm the person’s stated language preference and arrange appropriate support instead of substituting a country label.

bosnian.prompt: Separate a historical account in the reading from the information you actually need for a current invitation. Ask about access without asking the person to recount trauma.

amharic.prompt: Review whether a language-choice field accurately records the person’s own request, without treating a language as proof of nationality or identity.

french.prompt: A language appears across many places. How would you ask about the person’s actual language and format needs without assuming where they come from?

burmese.prompt: A country label appears in a referral. Confirm the individual’s requested language and interpreter arrangement instead of selecting one from the label.

khmer.prompt: Before a planning conversation, ask the person what communication and participation arrangements work, including whom they want involved.

chinese.prompt: A form offers only a broad language label. Ask which requested spoken, written or signed language and format work, then follow the appropriate support process.

colombian.prompt: An outreach invitation names a broad population but no feedback process. Ask partners how they prefer to contribute and explain how responses will be used.

cuban.prompt: Read a historical context statement, then write one question about the person’s present access needs that does not infer their migration history.

ecuadorian.prompt: Check whether a notice offers a way to request the preferred language or format; do not infer those preferences from national origin.

ethiopian.prompt: An intake form substitutes a nationality for language. Ask the individual which language and communication support they actually want.

filipino.prompt: Check whether a meeting invitation lets the person choose supporters, communication arrangements and time to respond, rather than assuming family roles.

guatemalan.prompt: A Spanish notice is available. Ask whether the person wants that language or a different language or format, then arrange support through the proper process.

indian.prompt: A broad identity label appears on a form. Ask the individual for the language and communication format needed for this task rather than inferring them.

japanese.prompt: Consider how your own preference for a fast verbal response shapes a meeting. Offer time or a written route and ask what works for the participant.

kenyan.prompt: An engagement team wants feedback on a proposed notice. Define the open decision, make participation usable and explain how comments will be considered.

korean.prompt: A person brings a supporter to a service conversation. Speak to the person directly and ask what role they want that supporter to have.

lao.prompt: Review a communication request for clarity and check the person’s stated language and format before selecting an interpreter or translated material.

lebanese.prompt: Separate language, national origin and religion in an outreach form. Ask only questions needed for access and do not infer one from another.

liberian.prompt: Before inviting community input, explain the purpose, usable participation options, any compensation process and how the team will report back.

mexican.prompt: Review whether a form can record a person’s name as they provide it. Ask how they would like to be addressed instead of assuming a naming pattern.

nigerian.prompt: Check whether a notice allows the person to request the specific language or communication format they prefer rather than assigning one from a broad label.

puerto-rican.prompt: Examine whether an outreach process offers accessible information and response options without making assumptions about a person’s language or background.

salvadoran.prompt: Plan an invitation with a clear purpose, open decision and accessible response route; explain what participants can influence and how you will follow up.

thai.prompt: A participant would like a supporter present. Ask how they want to communicate and make decisions, and clarify any actual authority requirements.

ukrainian.prompt: A reading gives historical context. Prepare an access question for today without assuming when, why or whether the person migrated.

vietnamese.prompt: Review an interpreter request and name field. Ask the person how their name should be recorded and what communication support they prefer.

native-american.prompt: Follow the standing deference for substantive questions and contact the people or areas responsible; a community reading does not replace a Nation’s own authority or consultation.

deaf-deafblind-hard-of-hearing.prompt: A projected caption screen is not usable for one participant. Ask what communication and access arrangements work and confirm that materials are usable too.
